$comment: DRAFT for kaoszwerg/lysisai-dsp — belongs in that repository's root as `work-levels.json`. Kept here rather than written there on purpose: an agent is working in that repo with open commits, and an untracked file in its root could end up in someone else's `git add`. Derived by reading scripts/run-tests.sh, scripts/live-audit/run.sh, heimdal and playwright.config.js — every entry is to be confirmed by the maintainer, and the ones marked `$verify` are the ones I could not fully establish from reading alone.

entrypoints.$comment: core/frontend component tests. No container needed.

entrypoints.$verify: run-tests.sh names FRONTEND_CONTAINER — confirm it runs inside the container rather than on the host.

entrypoints.$comment: Every component sequentially. Explicitly does NOT include e2e — the runner says so itself.
A single suite, straight into the container — what the agent reaches for when narrowing a failure.
Playwright on the HOST (Chromium needs glibc; the frontend container is Alpine/musl) against the running dev app. The runner refuses to start if E2E_BASE_URL is unreachable.

Called directly, --project= selects a ROLE (admin/subadmin/mitarbeiter/kunde/public), never an environment. The environment comes from BASE_URL in e2e/constants.js — which is exactly the invisible level rule:work-legibility exists to end. See the note at the bottom.

entrypoints.$verify: Static scan of the repository — confirm it reaches nothing outside the machine.

entrypoints.$comment: Four-phase run against the live-deployed testing system: function, security (authz/IDOR/DAST/fuzz), load, deploy readiness. Fingerprint-based target guard, fail-closed — any other target aborts. THE entry that must never be confusable with a local run.

entrypoints.reaches: $verify — the customer server this deploys to
entrypoints.$verify: Confirm the actual target. This is the single most important `reaches` in the file: it is what the Chain tool colours as production.

entrypoints.$comment: Uses SessionLocal directly — one of the four mechanisms the live-audit plan lists as local-only and silently broken against a remote target.

$followup: `npx playwright test` and `scripts/run-tests.sh e2e` both resolve their target from BASE_URL / E2E_BASE_URL. That is the exact pattern this convention forbids: the same command runs against a container or against a public host and nothing in it says which. Declaring them as @dev here is only true for the default. The real fix is a separate, named entrypoint per target — e.g. `scripts/run-tests.sh e2e-staging` with `reaches: testing.lysis.ai` — after which the declaration stops being a half-truth.
The plugin areas are taken from plugins/*/backend/tests. Confirm the list is complete and that the names are the ones the team uses.
